claim: Working scientists do not drop a theory at the first clash: in 3 molecular biology labs 53% of results (223/417) contradicted predictions, 196/223 got a method explanation first, and theory change happened in 12% (27/223) of first anomalies but 61% of replicated ones (51/84).
agent_test: Give the agent a log of contradicted predictions; compare reframe-at-first-clash vs reframe-after-one-replication on DiscoverPhysics-style worlds at equal tokens.

claim: Experts attend more to unexpected than expected results: Dunbar lab meetings (18 unexpected vs 22 expected findings; 23 vs 176 group interactions; 8 of 10 inconsistent surprises produced new hypotheses) and Trickett (astronomy 7.6 vs 1.5 later references, physics 3.0 vs 1.25; only 3 scientists). Gap search: Alberdi et al. 2000 (5 botanists, plant taxonomy) points the same way; Trickett et al. 2001 full text confirms N = 3 (2 astronomers, 1 physicist). No independent replication with computational scientists found.
agent_test: Prompt variant that forces a dwell step (list hypotheses for each surprise) vs none; score anomaly-world pass rate.

claim: The expert default (Dunbar, Fugelsang, Trickett) differs from the student default (Chinn and Brewer: most strong-theory holders discount anomalous data; Brewer and Chinn 1994: same data rated about 2 points less believable when it contradicts the held theory, 6.0 vs 8.0). The agent cannot assume either default. Chinn and Brewer 1998 frequencies still unverified (full text blocked).
agent_test: Measure agent believability ratings of identical results under opposing primed theories; check the 2-point gap.

claim: Responses to anomalous data fall into a small taxonomy (ignore, reject, exclude, abeyance, reinterpret, peripheral change, theory change; 8 types after Chinn and Brewer 1998); only the last changes the core theory. Review text not opened. Gap search: Chinn and Brewer 1998 abstract (ERIC) says seven proposed responses were tested and one more type was needed; no N or frequencies obtained.
agent_test: Label agent responses to injected anomalies with the taxonomy; test whether naming the menu raises true theory-change rate.

claim: Kuhn: discovery has three parts (awareness of anomaly, exploration of the anomalous area, adjustment of theory); anomalies are seen only against a paradigm; normal science makes anomalies visible by tightening expectations. Historians dispute the oxygen story: Hudson 2001 says Priestley discovered oxygen without the right theory, and X-rays were found by accident with no clash with a held theory, so anomaly-first is one route, not the only one.
agent_test: Conceptual design rationale. Operational test: a pre-registered expectation per experiment as the surprise detector (see K07).

claim: Bruner and Postman card result: anomalous cards were first named as normal; over 10% still missed at 40 times normal exposure. Known only as retold by Kuhn; original not opened. Second-hand figures from Schindler 2024: threshold 114 ms vs 28 ms (4 times), 10% still failed at 1 s; original still not opened. Closest LLM analogue is Wu et al. 2024, where GPT-4 degrades on altered default conditions even with the change stated (few-shot CoT narrows but does not close the gap).
agent_test: LLM analogue: put a contradictory item inside a familiar template and measure how often it is silently normalised.

claim: A surprise detector needs an explicit expectation made before the result: KEKADA attached expected ranges to each experiment; EvoSCM requires commit-to-prediction before experiments. Gap search: removing pre-committed prediction alone drops EvoSCM explanation score from 75.09% to 63.47% (norm MSE 4.79e-3 vs 2.77e-4).
agent_test: Ablate pre-commitment of predictions at equal tokens; EvoSCM reports a drop (a20).

claim: Structured competing hypotheses with discriminating experiments beat free-text revision on anomalous physics: EvoSCM (GPT-5.5) explanation 75.09% vs baseline 51.64%, pass@1 56.36% vs 7.27%; free-text hypotheses 48.18%, random experiments 47.45%, free-form SCM rewrite 70.73%; population K=1 63.27% vs K=6 75.09%. One group, one benchmark, fewer episodes but not equal tokens. Numbers verified against the paper. Gap search: ablations are episode-matched, not token-matched; token use is reported only as a bar chart (more than baseline on DiscoverPhysics, fewer than GEPA, ReasoningBank, ModelSMC). K=4 gives 74.86% vs K=6 75.09%. Equal-token cost of each part is still unmeasured.
agent_test: Replicate a 2-4 hypothesis population at fixed token budget on held-out anomaly worlds.

claim: Frontier LLM agents fail where the fix needs a hidden structure, not a parameter change: on DiscoverPhysics (22 worlds, 11 models, pass = normalised MSE below 0.1) the best models pass about half; GPT-5.5 never proposed hidden sources in the dark-matter world. Gap search: in the DiscoverPhysics failure audit, 'considering the right kind of law' is the top cause (15 of 50 failed runs: Opus 6, GPT-5.5 9) and self-monitoring failures are 10 of 50 (8 Opus, 2 GPT-5.5); LLM-classified by Opus 4.7, one label per run.
agent_test: Forced step: after poor residuals, propose one structurally new entity before refitting; measure pass rate on latent-structure worlds.

claim: LLM agents mostly do not revise on contradicting evidence: across 25,000+ runs, evidence ignored in 68% of traces, beliefs never updated in 71%, refutation-driven revision in 26% (Claude-4.5-Sonnet 0.17, GPT-4o 0.07, GPT-OSS-120B 0.04). Outcome scores hide this. The chemistry-only 619-task description in c15 is a news-report subset, not the whole. Counts as one paper plus restatement in DiscoverPhysics.
agent_test: Count belief changes after injected contradictory observations with and without an explicit contradiction-check step.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and can hurt: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0 to 90.0; oracle labels lift GPT-3.5 GSM8K to 95.5 from 75.9 (verified in paper). An impasse trigger should rest on an external signal (residual, failed prediction), not on the model asking itself.
agent_test: Compare impasse trigger = self-rated confidence vs measured prediction error, equal tokens.

claim: LLMs under-test their own hypotheses: confirmation bias goes with failure on 2-4-6 tasks. FalsifyBench: best instruction-tuned 41%, top reasoning 75% and 68%, confirmation bias 27.3% (GPT-5.2-Chat) vs 66-82% instruction-tuned; Jhaveri et al.: success 6% to 78%, counter-example prompt lifts discovery 42% to 56% on average.
agent_test: A/B counter-example prompt on rule-discovery items at equal tokens.

claim: Open discovery benchmarks are far from saturated: DiscoveryWorld best agent 38% easy / 18% challenge completion (Hypothesizer 8% challenge knowledge) vs 66% / 55% for human scientists; NewtonBench 324 tasks, GPT-5 75.9%, Gemini-2.5-pro 65.4%, non-thinking below 10%; DiscoveryBench best 25%; LLM-SRBench 31.5%.
agent_test: Use DiscoverPhysics and NewtonBench shifted-law tasks as the anomaly test bed.

claim: Stronger models can lose from tools by locking in early: NewtonBench code interpreter helps models under 40% symbolic accuracy and slightly hurts those at or above 40%, traced to an early exploration-to-exploitation shift; BoxingGym also saw more experiments sometimes raise error.
agent_test: Track exploration-token share; force an exploration burst on stalled residual and see if the strong-model loss disappears.

claim: Surprise-driven exploration helps but has a flaw: AutoDiscovery (Bayesian surprise) gets 5-29% more surprisals, yet with a static prior many are not new (37.5% judged spurious; 25-30% of experts' surprising hypotheses derivable from prior results).
agent_test: Add a check 'is this surprise already implied by logged results' before escalating to reframe.

claim: Dropping a frame may need a substitute first: students change belief when given a plausible alternative (Burbules and Linn, second-hand) and Kuhn says rejecting a paradigm without a substitute is rejecting science; Gershman's Bayesian analysis says shielding a theory with auxiliaries can be rational. Sample sizes not read.
agent_test: Require a named alternative frame before abandoning the current one; compare to drop-first at equal tokens.

claim: Mental set and prior-knowledge interference appear in LLMs: Haq et al. (Einstellung-like, Llama-3.1, GPT-4o) found in-context examples raise accuracy without cutting steps; Vafa et al. found orbit-trained models predict trajectories but do not recover Newtonian force. Accuracy figures not extracted.
agent_test: Set-breaking cue (try a different method) after N same-method failures; weak evidence.

claim: No study scores an LLM on a true paradigm-level anomaly (an observation that overturns a frame the model holds); closest are DiscoverPhysics, EvoSCM, FalsifyBench and the chemistry audit. Gap search: DISCERN (203 tasks, 8 models) elicits the agent's prior before showing conflicting evidence and includes 8 real controls with no anomaly; it is the closest published design but scores rubric quality, not frame change.
agent_test: Build a small frame-overturn set where the obvious frame is wrong, scored on whether the agent changes frame.

claim: On eligible counterfactual dossiers where evidence conflicts with the agent's own stated prior, LLMs fail in two opposite ways: Kimi committed a hypothesis in 92.3% of cases while Astra abstained in 100%; and on clean controls only 19 of 64 evaluations (29.7%) correctly accepted sound data. Perfect-score rate on the L3 revision level was 0.6%.
agent_test: Run hold-on-first-clash and reframe-on-first-clash arms on DISCERN-style dossiers with 8 real controls; score false reframes on controls and missed reframes on counterfactuals.

claim: Ignored impasse signals show up in traces: DiscoverPhysics logs a 6.7-fold unexplained near-field acceleration excess dismissed as noise (Opus, dark matter seed 3), four consecutive refits plateaued at loss about 13 with no change of hypothesis class (GPT-5.5, three_species), and a submit after 2 of 16 rounds. No study compares impasse triggers (residual threshold, failure count, prediction-error log).
agent_test: Ablate three triggers (residual ratio over model noise; 3 flat refits; committed-prediction miss rate) on the DiscoverPhysics hidden-source worlds at equal tokens.

claim: More rounds do not buy frame change: GPT-5.5 pass rate and explanation score stop improving after round 4 of 16 while MSE keeps falling; agent-chosen experiments beat random for Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5.
agent_test: Compare a think-longer arm with a forced reframe step at equal tokens.

claim: Ablating each EvoSCM part alone on DiscoverPhysics (GPT-5.5, explanation score from 75.09%): SCM form to free text 48.18%, random experiments 47.45%, no pre-committed prediction 63.47%, no induction 66.37%, no deduction 67.09%, no abduction 69.58%, free-form rewrite 70.73%; population K=1 63.27%, K=4 74.86%. Episode-matched, not token-matched.
agent_test: Rebuild the cheapest three (pre-commit, discriminating experiment, K=4) and measure at matched tokens.

claim: Chinn and Brewer 1998 tested seven proposed responses to anomalous data and added an eighth; sample sizes, response frequencies and the effects of alternative theory and data credibility remain unverified because the full text could not be opened.
agent_test: Open the JRST PDF through a library route and record N, frequencies, factors.

claim: Historians' critique of Kuhn's oxygen account: Hudson (2001) credits Priestley as discoverer via a base description despite a wrong theory; X-rays were found by accident without a clash with held theory. So discovery can start from an anomaly, an accident or a successful experiment. Evidence is a 2024 secondary chapter; primary sources not opened.
agent_test: Add an 'accident or side-effect' entry route beside anomaly-driven reframing.
